title: Server-Side Game Development
blurb: Multiplayer netcode (authoritative servers, prediction, interpolation, lag compensation) and game backends (matchmaking, fleets, economy, scaling).

quiz.question: In an authoritative server model, what should clients send?
options: Inputs; the server simulates and decides results
quiz.explanation: Never trust the client for outcomes.

quiz.question: Why do real-time games prefer UDP?
options: Avoids TCP head-of-line blocking; newest state matters more than late old state
quiz.explanation: Games add selective reliability on top of UDP.

quiz.question: What does client-side prediction with reconciliation do?
options: Applies local inputs immediately, then corrects from server state by replaying unacknowledged inputs

quiz.question: Why render remote players ~100 ms in the past?
options: To interpolate smoothly between received snapshots despite jitter and loss

quiz.question: What does lag compensation do for hitscan weapons?
options: Rewinds target hitboxes to what the shooter saw before testing hits

quiz.question: How should matchmaking balance quality and wait time?
options: Start with tight skill/latency windows and widen them as tickets wait

quiz.question: What prevents duplicated items when a client retries a purchase?
options: Idempotency keys with an atomic transaction for spend + grant + ledger

quiz.question: Which data structure is classic for leaderboards?
quiz.explanation: O(log n) updates and rank queries.

problems.title: Design 5v5 matchmaking
problems.prompt: Design matchmaking and server allocation for a 5v5 competitive game.
problems.solution: Tickets with party, MMR+uncertainty and region pings; per-mode/region queues; match function every 1–2 s balancing teams, widening windows with wait; allocate via Agones/managed fleet in best region with buffer autoscaling; match tokens; monitor wait time and match quality; Glicko-2/TrueSkill updates from server-reported results.
